chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man from our companions is too shy to take from the zakat. So can I give him from the zakat and not specify to him that it is from the zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give him and do not specify to him, and do not humiliate the believer.'
ai.seo_question: How should one give zakat to a shy recipient without embarrassing them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) validates the practice of *khiyanah* (hiding the source) in zakat distribution to protect the recipient's pride, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding social etiquette. This ruling underscores the principle that preserving the dignity of a believer (*la tuthill al-mu'min*) can take precedence over the strict disclosure of the fund's origin, reflecting the pragmatic and compassionate nature of Shia jurisprudence.
